title.value: Maximum State Entropy Exploration using Predecessor and Successor Representations
title.justification: The title clearly specifies the main focus of the study which is the exploration strategy using predecessor and successor representations.
title.quote: Maximum State Entropy Exploration using Predecessor and Successor Representations

extractions.description: This paper presents ηψ-Learning, an algorithm to learn efficient exploration policies in reinforcement learning by maximizing the entropy of the state visitation distribution through a single finite-length trajectory. The method combines predecessor and successor representations to optimize exploration efficiently in both discrete and continuous environments, aiming to achieve optimal state coverage with limited interactions.

primary_category.justification: The focus of this paper is primarily on reinforcement learning optimization techniques, specifically improving exploration algorithms, which does not directly relate to any environmental or eco-responsible initiatives.
primary_category.quote: This further requires an agent to carefully plan and account for the states that would follow after taking an action.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper is fundamentally about an exploration strategy in reinforcement learning, which is not aligned with typical eco-responsible themes or domains such as those addressing climate change, biodiversity, or pollution.
secondary_categories.quote: The core idea behind ηψ-Learning is the use of the predecessor and successor representations to predict the state visitation distribution induced by a non-Markovian policy for a single finite-length trajectory.

primary_sub_category.quote: To summarize, the contributions of this work are as follows: Firstly, we propose a mechanism to combine successor and predecessor representations for maximizing the entropy of the state visitation distribution.
